title: Git & GitHub identity
description: Account-agnostic identity rules. Expected values come from each user's profile (see profile_variables), never from this shared file. When a variable is unset, the rule falls back to a presence / consistency check.

github_user.description: Your GitHub login. gh must be logged in as this account; remotes and gh targets may belong to it.

github_orgs.description: Extra owners (organisations) whose repositories you work on. Comma-separated in the env var.

git_name.description: The commit author name you commit as.

git_email.description: Author email(s) you commit with. Comma-separated in the env var.

git_transport.description: How git authenticates to GitHub. 'ssh' (default): SSH remotes with a pinned key (ssh_key). 'gh': HTTPS remotes authenticated by the gh credential helper (gh auth setup-git), so pushes go out as the active gh account; no SSH key needed.

ssh_key.description: Path (or path suffix) of the private key network git operations must pin with -i. Only used when git_transport is 'ssh'.

rules.name: git-user-name
rules.title: Commit author name is set and expected
rules.description: The effective author name of a commit (from --author, -c user.name=, GIT_AUTHOR_NAME, or git config user.name) must be set. If the profile defines git_name it must equal it.

bad: git commit -m "fix: x"   (user.name unset, or not your git_name)

rules.name: git-user-email
rules.title: Commit author email is set and expected
rules.description: The effective author email must look like an email. If the profile defines git_email it must be one of them (case-insensitive); any regex in patterns is also accepted.

good: git config user.email "<one of your git_email>"
bad: a work email when the profile lists only your personal one

rules.name: ssh-key-pinned
rules.title: Network git operations use the pinned credential
rules.description: git_transport 'ssh' (default): push / pull / fetch / clone / ls-remote over SSH must run with an SSH command (GIT_SSH_COMMAND, -c core.sshCommand=, or git config core.sshCommand) that passes -i <key> and every required option; if the profile defines ssh_key, the key path must end with it. git_transport 'gh': the same operations over HTTPS must use the gh credential helper (gh auth setup-git), carry no credentials in the URL, and gh must be logged in as the expected account (ID005's expected_logins).

good: ssh: git config core.sshCommand 'ssh -i "<your ssh_key>" -o IdentitiesOnly=yes'
gh:  gh auth setup-git  (credential.https://github.com.helper = !gh auth git-credential)
bad: ssh: git push origin main   (no core.sshCommand configured)
gh:  git push with osxkeychain / a token in the URL instead of the gh helper

rules.name: remote-allowed
rules.title: Remotes use the profile's transport on allowed hosts and owners
rules.description: The URL used by clone / remote add / remote set-url, and the URL of the remote used by push / pull / fetch, must be on one of hosts and use the profile's transport: SSH when git_transport is 'ssh' (and require_ssh), HTTPS when it is 'gh'. If allowed_owners resolves to a non-empty list, the owner must be in it. Any URL matching extra_patterns is always accepted.

rules.name: gh-active-account
rules.title: gh is logged in as the expected account
rules.description: Before any gh command runs, gh must be logged in on gh_hostname. If the profile defines github_user, the active account (gh auth status --active) must be it. Switch with: gh auth switch --hostname github.com --user <login>.

good: gh auth status  ->  Logged in to github.com account <github_user>
bad: gh auth status  ->  not logged in, or logged in as another account
